donor_industry.caption: From itemized individual contributions over $200 reported to the FEC, grouped by the donor's self-reported employer and occupation. Employer means where the donor works, not that the company gave money; corporations can't give directly to campaigns. Industry groups use simple keyword rules and may misclassify some donors.
donor_industry.cycle_rule: House filings use the 2026 two-year cycle.

stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.
stands_for.scope: House roll calls 1–323 of 2026 (323 votes, January 6, 2026 to November 12, 2026), from the House Clerk.
stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.
stands_for.factual_flag: Not yet summarized: this line is built only from the official vote question and the bill's official title.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Concur in the Senate Amendments — AGOA Extension Act (H R 6500)
votes.bill_title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
votes.plain_language: The House voted to accept the Senate's rewrite of this bill, which became a stopgap that funds federal agencies into fiscal year 2027, generally through December 11, 2026, and extends several expiring programs. It is not a vote on the bill's original Africa-trade text. A two-thirds Yea accepts the Senate version; a Nay rejects it.

votes.bill_title: Establishing the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2027 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2028 through 2036.
votes.plain_language: This resolution sets federal budget targets for fiscal year 2027 through 2036 and instructs several House committees to write bills that would raise the deficit by limited amounts, which can move under faster reconciliation rules. A Yea adopts that budget plan. A Nay rejects it.

votes.plain_language: This bill provides FY2026 appropriations to several federal departments and agencies for activities and programs related to commerce, law enforcement, science, energy and water development, public lands, and the environment. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Retaining Divisions B and C — Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 6938)
votes.bill_title: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: H.R. 6938 combines three FY2026 spending bills: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment. The House voted separately on whether to keep parts of the bill. This vote was on keeping Divisions B and C. A Yea keeps them in the bill; a Nay would remove them.

votes.question: On Retaining Division A — Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 6938)
votes.bill_title: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: H.R. 6938 combines three FY2026 spending bills: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment. The House voted separately on whether to keep parts of the bill. This vote was on keeping Division A. A Yea keeps it in the bill; a Nay would remove it.

votes.question: On Passage — Sunshine Protection Act (H R 139)
votes.bill_title: Sunshine Protection Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: This bill makes daylight saving time the new, permanent standard time. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Lulu’s Law (S 1003)
votes.bill_title: Lulu’s Law
votes.plain_language: This bill requires the Federal Communications Commission to issue an order explicitly permitting the transmission of wireless emergency alerts to mobile phones in the event of a shark attack. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Kari’s Law Reporting Act (H R 5201)
votes.bill_title: Kari's Law Reporting Act
votes.plain_language: This bill requires the Federal Communications Commission to publish a report on the enforcement of Kari’s Law, which requires multiline telephone systems to be preconfigured to allow users to dial 9-1-1 directly from any phone without dialing any additional code or prefix. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Emergency Reporting Act (H R 5200)
votes.bill_title: Emergency Reporting Act
votes.plain_language: This bill requires the Federal Communications Commission to investigate and report on emergency communications outages (e.g., 9-1-1 outages). This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Expediting Federal Broadband Deployment Reviews Act (H R 1681)
votes.bill_title: Expediting Federal Broadband Deployment Reviews Act
votes.plain_language: This bill establishes an interagency strike force to support federal land management agencies' review of requests for communications use authorizations. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Motion to Recommit — Take Care of America’s Veterans Act (H R 9237)
roll_calls.plain_language: H.R. 9237 (Take Care of America’s Veterans Act) addresses veterans’ benefits, health care, counseling, Department of Veterans Affairs personnel, VA infrastructure, and the Veterans Community Care Program. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
